name: Coresight Research on AI in Retail: Groceryshop 2026 and Personalization
title: Coresight Research on AI in Retail: Groceryshop 2026 and Personalization
answer: Coresight Research is a retail research firm whose site publishes event coverage and analyst reports on AI in retail. Its Groceryshop 2026 coverage is the most useful material, describing how grocery retailers such as Kroger, Instacart and Albert Heijn are moving AI shopping assistants from pilots into daily execution, and arguing that AI's main value lies in reducing shoppers' decision effort rather than expanding choice.

sections.body: Coresight Research is a retail research firm publishing analyst reports and event coverage on its website. The material read covers its Groceryshop 2026 coverage, published as a day one report, a day two report, a day three report and a wrap-up, plus a report on AI in marketing personalization. Groceryshop 2026 took place on September 22 to 24 at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas, Nevada, and Coresight Research states it was a research partner of the event. The reports are written for retail and consumer packaged goods professionals and mix conference session summaries with Coresight's own analysis.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The Groceryshop coverage describes grocery retail moving from AI pilots into day-to-day execution. AI assistants are shifting shopping from item-by-item search toward intent-driven experiences that build full baskets around a single stated need, such as meal planning, dietary requirements, budgets and household preferences. Instacart is using AI to let shoppers express broader needs, Kroger is creating baskets from photos, recipes and personalization signals, and Albert Heijn is expanding its assistant from meal inspiration into personalized meal planning, pre-filled baskets and service tasks such as coupon activation. Schnuck Markets found that an effective assistant required significant data preparation, including better nutritional and promotion data and structured internal expertise. Coresight argues the advantage from AI will come less from individual tools than from rebuilding end-to-end processes around speed, trust and human oversight, and that scaling requires adoption across customers, employees, infrastructure and governance. Discovery quality depends on product data, inventory accuracy and digital shelf readiness. Retailers are moving toward one-to-one personalization based on intent and occasion, and as AI agents become a shopping interface, proprietary capabilities around customer data and loyalty are framed as protection against disintermediation. Value is being redefined beyond price through quality, convenience, private label and health, including food-as-medicine programs and membership schemes.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: Groceryshop 2026 took place on September 22 to 24 at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas, Nevada, and Coresight Research was a research partner. The day two report says sessions were categorized into six major themes. The wrap-up says AI lets retailers launch targeted campaigns within minutes rather than days. It also says brands manage millions of data points across retailers, SKUs, content formats and performance signals. The reports name companies including Albertsons, Ahold Delhaize, Kroger, Instacart, Loblaw, Sam's Club, Schnuck Markets, Thrive Market, Uber, Adobe, Amazon.com, Marks and Spencer, Salesforce and The Home Depot.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in retail gets a compact, current account of where grocery AI has moved beyond experimentation. The reports name specific retailers and describe concrete uses, from basket building to demand sensing and retail media, and they identify the operational conditions, data quality, governance and process redesign, that determine whether assistants work. The marketing personalization report extends this to unified customer profiles, next-best-action decisioning and real-time content. Together they give a practitioner both vendor-neutral examples and a framework for judging AI claims.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Retail

sections.body: The material is conference coverage and analyst commentary rather than primary data, and much of it reports what speakers said rather than independently verified results. The Groceryshop reports are tied to a single event and its sessions, so they reflect the agendas of participating retailers and vendors. The marketing personalization report is descriptive and names technology suppliers, and the site also carries commercial research offerings. No adoption rates or market sizing figures appear in the pages read.
